title: API contract shrinkwrap playbook and regen samples
author: Sofia Nguyen
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents the operational steps, automated scripts, and canonical example fixes used when an upstream API contract change is detected (breaking or additive) that requires a shrinkwrap (pinning) or regeneration of SDKs, updates to the docs site, and publishing a canonical support fix. It is intended for oncall engineers, SDK owners, Docs engineers, and DX support triage.

Goals:
- Limit customer-facing breakage by applying shrinkwraps or compatibility layers quickly.
- Provide reproducible regeneration steps and tests so SDK authors can ship safe fixes.
- Record canonical fixes so support can quickly apply patches or rollbacks.

When to use this playbook:
- A breaking change is introduced in the Redwood API (route rename, parameter removal, response schema change) that fails customer integration tests or triggers high-severity support tickets.
- Automated compatibility tests (contract CI) fail for one or more SDK languages.
- Docs examples render incorrectly in the live docs site or snippet test harness fails.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Primary owner: SDK Runtime Team (engineering)
- Secondary owners: DX Docs (eng-developer-experience), Developer Support (customer-success)
- Initial triage SLA: 30 minutes from Pager duty alert (P0 means page)
- Patch or rollback target: < 4 hours for high-impact customers; < 24 hours for non-P0 regressions

Severity classification table:
| Severity | Symptoms | Action | Target TAT |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| P0 | Production customers unable to call API (500s, missing required fields) | Emergency page, hotfix shrinkwrap + docs note | 4 hours |
| P1 | Feature regression (incorrect outputs, warnings) | Regenerate SDK, run golden tests, documentation update | 24 hours |
| P2 | Additive change, minor examples fail | Schedule for next SDK patch, add compatibility-note | 7 days |

Triage procedure (step-by-step):
1. Confirm the failure: reproduce the failing call using the API CLI and one of the official SDKs. Record the request/response.
2. Check contract CI: open the CI job dashboard at /ci/contracts and identify which git commit introduced the failing spec.
3. Determine scope: is this a server-side intentional change or an accidental break? Tag the API/product owner in the contract issue.
4. If server-side intentional and backward-incompatible, create a temporary compatibility shim and open a shrinkwrap PR for SDKs (see Shrinkwrap section).
5. If accidental, coordinate rollback with the rollout owner, then follow the rollback checklist below.

Shrinkwrap (pin) quick recipe:
- Purpose: prevent new transitive dependency or autogenerated client changes from breaking downstream code while a regeneration is prepared.
- High level: pin the codegen schema + generator version in repo and publish a patch release that uses the pinned artifact.

Commands and example (TypeScript):
1) Pin the schema and codegen commit in the SDK repo: 
   git checkout -b shrinkwrap/api-2026-01-12
   cp /tmp/reprobed_schema/openapi.json docs/schemas/openapi-shrinkwrap-20260112.json
   git add docs/schemas/openapi-shrinkwrap-20260112.json && git commit -m "chore(shrinkwrap): pin schema for api change 2026-01-12"

2) Update generator configuration (example node script snippet):
   node ./scripts/generate-client.js --schema docs/schemas/openapi-shrinkwrap-20260112.json --template stable

3) Run local smoke tests and golden diff: 
   ./scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh --language typescript --golden tests/goldens/typescript

4) Publish patch (after approvals): 
   npm version patch && npm publish --access public 

Regeneration procedure (full regen):
- Use when the change is intentional and SDKs should adopt the new contract.
- Steps:
  1) Update authoritative schema at /infra/contracts/openapi.json (product/API owner PR required).
  2) Run codegen for each supported language in the regen matrix (see matrix below).
  3) Run full integration suite: unit, golden, smoke, E2E against staging.
  4) Submit SDK PRs with CHANGELOG and migration notes.
  5) Coordinate docs update PRs to include new example snippets and migration guidance.
  6) Release SDKs and update docs snippets in the docs-site pipeline.

Language regen matrix (example):
| Language | Generator | Smoke target | Required tests |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| TypeScript | openapi-generator-typescript (stable) | examples/ts/smoke.js | unit, golden, snippets-runner |
| Python | openapi-python-client | examples/py/smoke.py | unit, golden, snippets-runner |
| Go | openapi-generator-go | examples/go/smoke.go | unit, golden |
| Java | openapi-generator-java | examples/java/SmokeApp | unit, integration |

Canonical fixes cookbook (examples):
- Missing optional field tolerated by server but generated as required in SDK: add a compatibility wrapper that maps missing -> default and publish shrinkwrap patch.
- Renamed enum value: add a translation table in the SDK and mark as deprecated; raise lint rule to error in next major.
- Response shape changed from {meta: {...}} to {meta: null}: add defensive parsing and a golden test that asserts both shapes handled.

Docs site flow for snippet changes:
1. Update code sample snippets inline with SDK changes in the code snippet repo (docs/snippets).
2. Run snippet test harness locally: 
   ./tools/snippet-runner --env staging --report out/snippet-report.json
3. If tests fail because of API changes, tag docs-oncall and open a docs emergency PR with the snippet update.
4. Use the docs-site hotpatch pipeline for urgent fixes: create branch docs-hotfix/api-shrinkwrap-YYYYMMDD and follow the hotpatch checklist.

Hotpatch checklist (docs-site):
1. Branch from live-main.
2. Update snippet and add a single-line banner in the affected page: "Known API change on <date>; an SDK patch is available."
3. Run smoke: yarn build:prod && ./tools/serve-static --port 4005 and confirm sample page renders.
4. Open PR, request reviewers: @docs-team, @sdk-owner.
5. Merge and trigger the hotpatch deploy job.
6. Post link to runbook channel and update status page if customer-facing.

Rollback checklist (when server rollback is chosen):
1. Confirm rollback window and impact with product owner.
2. Revert rollout in deployment system: kubectl rollout undo ... (or cloud deploy revert).
3. Verify contract CI green; then merge a revert commit in SDK repos that removes compatibility shim.
4. Publish docs note describing rollback and next steps.

Testing and observability guidance:
- Add a contract compatibility test in CI that runs the following for each language: generate client from authoritative schema, run smoke examples, run golden diff using snippets-runner.
- Add a Docs snippet regression job that mirrors public docs rendering: runs snippet-runner and failures open an alert in PagerDuty for docs-oncall.
- Telemetry: emit an event `contract.regression.detected` when the CI contract job fails. Include fields: repo, language, failing-endpoint, commit.

Example canonical fix patch (TypeScript compatibility wrapper):
```ts
// compatibility-wrapper.ts
export function safeParseList(resp: any) {
  if (!resp) return [];
  // older servers returned {items: null}
  if (resp.items == null) return [];
  return Array.isArray(resp.items) ? resp.items : [resp.items];
}
```
Include this wrapper in the SDK and add a golden test asserting both old/new shapes.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Internal incident note (Slack): "P0: API contract break detected at 11:08 UTC affecting /v1/generate. Triage in progress. SDK teams paged. Temporary shrinkwrap PR opened: <link>. Follow playbook: api-contract-shrinkwrap. Owner: @sofia.nguyen."
- Customer-facing status (Statuspage): "We’re investigating an issue affecting API compatibility for some SDK versions. A patch is being rolled out; temporary workarounds are available in our developer docs."

Post-incident follow-up (1–2 weeks):
- Generate an incident retrospective and include: root cause, timeline, what worked, what failed, outstanding action items (who, due date).
- Add a new contract regression golden to the appropriate repo.
- If tooling gaps were found, open engineering tickets for: faster snippet testing, improved codegen stability, or CI flakiness.

Related resources and scripts:
- Contract CI dashboard: /ci/contracts
- Snippet runner: /tools/snippet-runner
- SDK regen scripts: /infra/scripts/regen-all.sh
- Docs hotpatch job: docs/hotpatch-quickdeploy.yml

Appendix: quick-reference commands
- Local regen (TS): node ./scripts/generate-client.js --schema /infra/contracts/openapi.json --out dist/ts
- Run TS smoke: node examples/ts/smoke.js
- Publish shrinkwrap patch: npm version patch && npm publish

End of playbook.
Notes: keep this page updated when new languages are added to the regen matrix, or when the hotpatch pipeline changes. For questions, contact the SDK runtime team or the docs-oncall rotation.
